name: TomP2P
tagline: Java DHT library: a Kademlia-style peer-to-peer key-value store; archived and unmaintained.
description: TomP2P is a Java library implementing a distributed hash table: every peer keeps a memory- or disk-backed table, and keys are routed to the closest peers with XOR-based iterative routing similar to Kademlia. On top of put/get it adds operations such as putIfAbsent, add, digests, Bloom-filtered gets, replication and signed data, plus NAT traversal via UPnP and NAT-PMP, all exposed through non-blocking futures on Netty. It came out of the University of Zurich and powered research and some P2P applications. The 5.0 line never left beta (last tag 5.0-Beta8.1, May 2020) and the GitHub repository is now archived.
statusNote: GitHub repo archived; last tag 5.0-Beta8.1 (May 2020) and tomp2p.net is offline. No maintained successor.
developer: Thomas Bocek and contributors (University of Zurich)

scale.notes: Peers join an overlay network; data is spread and replicated across peers by key distance.

strengths: Complete DHT stack in one library: routing, replication, NAT traversal and signed data
Non-blocking API built on Netty futures
Extended operations (Bloom-filter gets, digests, custom RPCs) beyond plain put/get
weaknesses: Archived; 5.0 never reached a stable release
Eventual consistency only, with no transactions or query language
Documentation site is gone and examples target old APIs
